privacy.ai_training_note: Hemingway states on its Plus page: 'We will never sell your data, let others use it to train an AI, or use it for advertising.' Hemingway Editor Plus's AI features (rewrites, tone, grammar) send text to OpenAI's API. Per OpenAI's API data usage policy (effective March 1, 2023), data submitted via the API is not used to train or improve OpenAI models unless the customer explicitly opts in; API logs may be retained up to 30 days for abuse monitoring and are then deleted. This is consistent with Hemingway's no-training pledge, so the earlier 'contradiction' framing was not supported. The free web and desktop versions analyze text locally in the browser with no server transmission. Users handling sensitive content should still note that Plus AI features transmit text to OpenAI as a subprocessor.

flags: AI FEATURES USE OPENAI (NO CONTRADICTION): Hemingway Editor Plus sends text to OpenAI's API for AI rewrites, tone, and grammar. Per OpenAI's API data usage policy, API-submitted data is not used to train OpenAI models unless the customer opts in, so this is consistent with Hemingway's pledge that it will not 'let others use it to train an AI.' Note only that AI features transmit text off-device to OpenAI; OpenAI is not named on the Plus page.

The privacy policy and terms of service exist but are not easily accessible at standard URLs (no /privacy, /terms, or /legal pages). They are referenced in the login flow but difficult for users to discover or review upfront.
No formal trust center, security page, or compliance documentation is published, and there is no transparency report on security practices or incident response.
No Data Processing Agreement is published, so GDPR-regulated customers cannot easily comply with Article 28 requirements.

Despite privacy-forward messaging, the company holds no SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, or other formal compliance certifications. This is typical for growth-stage indie tools but limits enterprise adoption.
Third-party analytics tools collect IP address and browser type, and an external review has noted cookie usage for analytics and potentially targeted advertising.
The vendor does not document where data is stored or processed, which is critical for GDPR, HIPAA, or international data protection compliance.

Text submitted to Plus AI features is processed by OpenAI's API under OpenAI's data policy (no training on API data by default; up to 30-day abuse-monitoring retention, then deletion). This is a subprocessor relationship worth noting during procurement, not a violation of Hemingway's privacy claims.
